strengths: The paper addresses a useful problem with an identifiable audience in representation learning and program analysis. Aligning source code, generated comments, and LLVM representations is a plausible approach, and the architecture diagrams communicate the overall training pipeline.

The reported results are encouraging on several tasks: function-name accuracy increases from 29.41 to 33.41, and summarization BLEU-4 increases from GraphCodeBERT’s 32.43 to 34.36. Evaluating both discriminative and generative tasks provides useful breadth.

The experiments examine relevant design choices, including frozen encoders, comment inclusion, generated versus human-written comments, and adaptation to CodeT5. These investigations could support an informative empirical contribution once the concerns below are resolved.
weaknesses: Necessary—resolve the evaluation protocol. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify non-overlapping POJ-104 problem labels across training, development, and test sets, whereas Section 4.2 describes supervised classification into 104 classes. An ordinary classifier cannot learn held-out classes under this setup. If the experiment actually measures retrieval or similarity, specify the training objective, candidate pools, ranking procedure, and metric definitions. Section 3.2 also says generation is evaluated on validation data, while Section 4.3 calls these test-set results. These inconsistencies prevent confident interpretation of the reported scores.

Necessary—align the binary-analysis claims with the evaluated inputs. The experiments use compiler-generated LLVM IR obtained from source code, rather than representations recovered from stripped executables. Figures 7–8 retain informative function and type names. Such IR is not trivially interchangeable with stripped machine code, as the introductory footnote claims. Either provide evidence for the intended stripped-binary setting or narrow the paper’s claims to the LLVM setting actually studied and document retained symbols and compiler settings.

Necessary—isolate the contribution of interpolation. The primary-contrastive baseline receives 10 pretraining epochs, versus 30 or 70 for the full method. Consequently, its weaker performance does not establish that interpolation causes the improvement. Section 5.1 states that the shorter baseline converged but supplies no supporting learning curves. A matched-budget comparison and controls separating interpolation variants and training order are needed to substantiate the proposed components’ benefits.

Necessary—make the method reproducible. Equation 4 omits the softmax described in the surrounding text, leaving Equation 5’s cross-entropy targets incompletely specified. Whether gradients propagate through those targets also matters because they depend on the trainable embeddings. The instruction to randomly select any two modalities needs reconciliation with the frozen source/comment encoder and the binary-versus-anchor equations. Specify the exact loss, gradient paths, encoder pooling, interpolation network, generation decoder, and preprocessing configuration.

Necessary—support or narrow claims of semantic correctness. BLEU, GLEU, and exact match measure reference agreement and do not establish functional equivalence or reliable comprehension. The comments are generated by CodeT5, so their use as summarization references requires explicit disclosure and an independent correctness assessment. No execution-based decompilation evaluation or systematic human assessment supports the stronger conclusions. Figure 8 even displays an incomplete shift expression in a highlighted generated program. Provide appropriate semantic validation or restrict conclusions to the measured text-generation outcomes.

Necessary—correct overinterpretation of the evidence. Section 4.1 argues that unique programs should not cluster and that the t-SNE visualization proves embedding quality; neither inference is valid. Distinct programs can share semantics, and distances across separately fitted t-SNE plots are not directly comparable. Likewise, Table 6 shows lower BLEU than GraphCodeBERT and only a 0.43 percentage-point exact-match advantage, without uncertainty estimates. Claims of consistent superiority and robustness should reflect these mixed results. Document split construction and overlap checks for the GitHub-derived corpora; the manuscript does not establish leakage, but it provides insufficient information to assess independence.

Optional—streamline repetitive motivation, repair unresolved citations and cross-references, and standardize terminology such as GLEU/GLUE and DIRE/DIRT/DIRTY. The central idea is understandable, but these presentation issues make the experimental account harder to follow.
